title: Programmatic Argument Permutation Helpers
pattern: Writing custom procedurally interpreted permutation code to re-order standard API arguments for a single localized use case.
why_bad: It introduces unnecessary abstraction layers and run-time interpretation costs for simple arguments shuffling.
detection: A routine whose sole purpose is to capture arguments, re-order them, and forward them to another callable.
counterexample: Creating a generic combinator library designed to handle late-bound functions specialization.
fix: Use a simple lambda closure/anonymous function wrapper to bind and re-order the arguments statically.
source: *Software Design for Flexibility (Hanson & Sussman), Chapter 2, p. 10 [10]*
